This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

Melody

Melody is a small language for authoring readable patterns that compile to ECMAScript regular expressions.

Examples

16 of "na";

2 of match {
  <space>;
  "batman";
}

Turns into:

(?:na){16}(?: batman){2}

"#";
some of <word>;

Turns into:

#\w+

CLI Usage

USAGE:
    melody [OPTIONS] [INPUT_FILE_PATH]

ARGS:
    <INPUT_FILE_PATH>    Read from a file; use '-' or pipe input to read from stdin

OPTIONS:
    -f, --test-file <TEST_FILE>    Test the compiled regex against the contents of a file
        --generate-completions <COMPLETIONS>    Output shell completions
    -h, --help    Print help information
    -n, --no-color    Print output with no color
    -o, --output <OUTPUT_FILE_PATH>    Write to a file
    -r, --repl    Start the Melody REPL
    -t, --test <TEST>    Test the compiled regex against a string
    -V, --version    Print version information

File extensions

Melody source files typically use the .mdy or .melody extension.

Syntax (summary)

Quantifiers:
- `... of` - exact amount
- `... to ... of` - range
- `some of` - 1 or more
- `any of` - 0 or more
- `option of` - 0 or 1

Symbols:
- `<char>` - any character
- `<space>` - a space character
- `<whitespace>` - any whitespace
- `<digit>` - any digit
- `<word>` - word character (letters, digits, underscore)

def run(args, sends, env=None):

  if env: os.environ.update(env)

 out=b''

use builtin;
use str;

set edit:completion:arg-completer[melody] = {|@words|
    fn spaces {|n|
        builtin:repeat $n ' ' | str:join ''
    }
    fn cand {|text desc|
        edit:complex-candidate $text &display=$text' '(spaces (- 14 (wcswidth $text)))$desc

using namespace System.Management.Automation
using namespace System.Management.Automation.Language

Register-ArgumentCompleter -Native -CommandName 'melody' -ScriptBlock {
    param($wordToComplete, $commandAst, $cursorPosition)

    $commandElements = $commandAst.CommandElements
    $command = @(
        'melody'
        for ($i = 1; $i -lt $commandElements.Count; $i++) {
            $element = $commandElements[$i]
            if ($element -isnot [StringConstantExpressionAst] -or
                $element.StringConstantType -ne [StringConstantType]::BareWord -or
                $element.Value.StartsWith('-') -or
                $element.Value -eq $wordToComplete) {
                break
        }
        $element.Value
    }) -join ';'

    $completions = @(switch ($command) {
        'melody' {
            [CompletionResult]::new('-o', '-o', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Write to a file')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--output', '--output', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Write to a file')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--generate-completions', '--generate-completions', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Outputs completions for the selected shell To use, write the output to the appropriate location for your shell')
            [CompletionResult]::new('-t', '-t', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Test the compiled regex against a string')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--test', '--test', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Test the compiled regex against a string')
            [CompletionResult]::new('-f', '-f', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Test the compiled regex against the contents of a file')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--test-file', '--test-file', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Test the compiled regex against the contents of a file')
            [CompletionResult]::new('-n', '-n', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Print output with no color')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--no-color', '--no-color', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Print output with no color')
            [CompletionResult]::new('-r', '-r', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Start the Melody REPL')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--repl', '--repl', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Start the Melody REPL')
            [CompletionResult]::new('-h', '-h', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Print help')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--help', '--help', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Print help')

import unittest
from melody.regex import Regex, RegexError


class RegexTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_search_and_repetition(self):
        self.assertTrue(Regex('(?:ab){2,4}').search('xababx'))
        self.assertFalse(Regex('^(?:ab){2,4}$').search('xababx'))
        self.assertTrue(Regex('^(?:ab){2,4}$').search('ababab'))

    def test_assertions(self):
        self.assertTrue(Regex('(?<=a+)b(?=c)').search('aabc'))
        self.assertFalse(Regex('(?<!a)b').search('ab'))
        self.assertTrue(Regex('a(?!b)').search('ac'))

    def test_characters(self):
        self.assertTrue(Regex(r'\w+').search('a_0'))
        self.assertFalse(Regex(r'\w+').search('é'))
        self.assertTrue(Regex(r'\uD83D\uDE00').search('😀'))
        self.assertTrue(Regex('^.$').search('😀'))
        self.assertFalse(Regex('^.$').search('\n'))
        self.assertTrue(Regex('^[^]$').search('\n'))
        self.assertFalse(Regex('[]').search('a'))

    def test_empty_and_boundaries(self):
        self.assertTrue(Regex('').search(''))
        self.assertTrue(Regex(r'\b?').search(' '))
        self.assertTrue(Regex('(?:)+').search(''))
        self.assertFalse(Regex('a$').search('a\n'))

    def test_captures(self):
        self.assertTrue(Regex('(?<part>ab)c').search('abc'))
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RegexError, 'duplicate capture group name'):
            Regex('(?<part>a)(?<part>b)')

    def test_regex_diagnostics(self):
        for source, cause in [('[','unbalanced bracket'), ('(','unbalanced parenthesis'),
                              ('a{3,2}','invalid quantifier'), ('*a','invalid atom character'),
                              ('^*','quantifier not allowed here')]:
            with self.subTest(source=source), self.assertRaises(RegexError) as failure:
                Regex(source)
            self.assertEqual(str(failure.exception),cause)

    def test_long_literal(self):
        text = 'abc'*1500
        self.assertTrue(Regex('^'+text+'$').search(text))
